transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been kind of unable to stop starting things. Like at work I’ll make these big plans, then I’m setting up certification schedules, then I’m upgrading things at home, messaging old contacts… it just keeps going. It gets intense enough that I blow past normal limits, and then my wife or my director has to step in and slow me down.
Have you noticed yourself often interrupting others or finishing their sentences when you're talking to them?
I’m not sure. I don’t really notice myself finishing people’s sentences. I might jump in sometimes if I’m excited, but I can’t say it’s a regular thing.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Yes, very easily. If my phone buzzes or a fan makes a clicking sound, or even if someone just walks past my office door, my attention goes straight to that. Then I’ll realize I’ve completely stopped working on the report or ticket I was supposed to finish.
Do you often act on impulse without much consideration for the consequences?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as acting without any thought, but there are times I decide quickly and move on it before I’ve really sat with it. I guess I’d need to think about examples.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yes. I get pretty restless sitting still. If I’m supposed to just sit and watch a show, I start feeling physically uncomfortable, like I need to get up. I’ll pace around the house with my laptop, or I’ll suddenly start reorganizing the garage or rewriting project boards instead of just staying seated.
Do you often have mood swings?

Yes, I do. Some weeks I feel really up, almost electric, like I can handle anything and I don’t want to slow down. But then something small, like a delay or my wife asking me a simple question, can set me off. I’ll snap because it feels like people are getting in my way on purpose, even if I know later that’s probably not fair.
Do you often talk excessively, to the point where others have trouble getting a word in?

I’m not sure. I don’t really notice myself doing that a lot. I can talk more when I’m worked up or focused on something, but I don’t know if it’s to the point where people can’t get a word in. No one has really told me that directly.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or having trouble sitting still in most situations, like at work, at home, or in social settings?

Yeah, mostly at home, but it can happen in other places too. At home it’s the most obvious—I’ll try to sit and watch a show and I start feeling physically uncomfortable, like I need to move. I’ll end up pacing around with my laptop, or going off to reorganize the garage, or rewriting project boards instead of just sitting still.
Have your symptoms or behaviors caused problems for you at work, at home, or in your relationships?

Yes. It’s caused real problems. At work, I was put on leave after a migration failed, and that was… pretty hard to face.

At home, my wife has had to step in more than she should—around spending, me working late at night, and conversations turning into arguments. And I’ve pulled back from things I used to be involved in, like church music, climbing, and mentoring, because I can’t reliably show up or follow through.
Have you experienced these restlessness and impulsivity symptoms consistently over the past few months?

Yes, over the past few months it’s been pretty consistent. It’s like I can’t stop starting things—work plans, certification schedules, home network upgrades, even reaching out to old contacts. I’ll get locked in and push past normal limits, and then my wife or my director has to step in and tell me to stop or pull back.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt abnormally happy or irritable for several days or longer?

Yes. There are stretches, sometimes for weeks, where I feel almost electric—like I’m unstoppable and everything is moving too slowly around me. But it can flip into irritation really fast. Like if my wife asks a question or there’s some small delay, I can snap because it feels like people are trying to slow me down on purpose.
Have you had any periods in your life where these symptoms, such as restlessness and impulsivity, were not present or were significantly less severe?

Yes. There have been calmer stretches, like a few weeks at a time, where I wasn’t really up or depressed. The restlessness and impulsive stuff was much less intense then.

But even during those flatter periods, I still had some of the other things going on—like thinking Teams statuses were coded warnings, or hearing brief comments when no one was actually there.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder?
I don’t think so. I’ve never had an ADHD diagnosis that I’m aware of, and I haven’t been treated specifically for that.
Do you often have difficulty completing tasks or projects because you lose interest or get bored with them?

Yes, that happens. It’s not always just boredom, but I’ll lose interest in things I normally care about. Like I used to look forward to grilling, climbing, playing music at church, helping mentor the robotics kids… and then for months I just don’t care. I’ll let messages sit unanswered and projects kind of fade out because I can’t make myself feel interested in them.
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work or other activities?

Yes. Especially when I’m more keyed up, little things pull me off track. If my phone buzzes, or the fan clicks, or someone walks past my office door, my attention just snaps to that, and then I’ll realize I’ve abandoned the report or ticket I was supposed to finish.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was consistently depressed for at least two weeks?
Yes. I’ve had stretches like that where for weeks I wake up feeling like a failed version of myself. Just heavy and flat. Even answering normal questions from my wife can feel like too much.
Have you ever engaged in reckless behavior that could have caused harm to yourself or others?
Not really, no. I can’t think of a time where I did something reckless that put me or someone else in danger. At least nothing that stands out to me like that.

Have you ever had a comprehensive evaluation for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder that included an assessment of your symptoms across different settings, such as at home, in school, or at work?

No, I don’t think I’ve had anything that thorough. I’ve talked about attention problems here and there, but I don’t remember doing a full evaluation that looked at home, school, and work all together.
Have you often had difficulty organizing tasks and activities?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I have normal days where keeping things in order is annoying, but I don’t know that I’d say it’s often or a major pattern. Nothing specific comes to mind.
Have you often had difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities?

Yes, I do. If I’m working on a report or a ticket, even something small like my phone buzzing, a fan clicking, or someone walking past my office door can pull my attention away. I’ll snap to that and then realize I’ve basically abandoned what I was supposed to be finishing.
